newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Anglo-Argentine Falkland talks get mixed reviews.
newsitem.headline: Anglo-Argentine Falkland talks get mixed reviews.

text.p: Argentina's two leading newspapers were unable to agree on Sunday on the outcome of the latest round of Anglo-Argentine talks over the disputed Falkland islands, with one citing progress and the other failure.

"Meeting on sovereignty in London a failure," said La Nacion, referring to the talks on Friday and Saturday between British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind and his Argentine counterpart Guido Di Tella.

"Government says there is progress on Malvinas," said the banner headline of the mass-circulation daily Clarin. Argentina calls the disputed sparsely-populated islands in the South Atlantic, Malvinas.

A Foreign Office spokesman said on Saturday in London that the two ministers discussed the Falklands, over which Argentina and Britain fought a bloody 10-week war in 1982, but came to no particular conclusions and no further meetings were planned.
Britain said before the talks began that there could be no question of it offering to share or transfer sovereignty of the islands to Argentina.
La Nacion highlighted the inconclusive talks and London's denial to discuss sovereignty to back up its negative reading.

But Clarin quoted Argentine government officials as saying they were getting "positive signals" from British officials and those signals led President Carlos Menem to talk in recent days of the possibility of shared sovereignty over the islands.
Foreign Ministry sources described the Rifkind-Di Tella talks as "the most important (meeting on Falklands) in the last 20 years," Clarin said.
